why: At 0:22-0:24 the silver car (left) and red car (right) sit nose-to-nose with a small gap and both hoods open. The video doesn't show the 18-inch figure, but it's standard guidance.

At 0:18-0:20 the key is turned (off). 0:26 shows the selector at P (yellow P lit), 0:28 the hand at the console, and 0:30 a finger presses the start/stop button. The span 26.5-32 covers P and off. The key shot at 0:18 comes before the span but is short.
At 0:32 the red clamp goes onto the post with the red + sticker on the felt-wrapped battery of the silver (dead) VW.

edits.say: In the red car, flip open the small black cover marked with a red plus on top of the fuse box. Clip the other red clamp onto the metal positive jump post under it.
placements: other red clamp → positive (+) jump post under the small flip-up black cover marked with a red + on the fuse box, beside the coolant reservoir in the red working car, jaws fully closed on the post

why: At 0:34 the hand lifts a small black cover with a red + on the fuse-box lid. At 0:36-0:38 the red clamp grips the metal post under it. It is a remote + jump post, not the battery itself, so the wording should send the learner to the red-+ cover.
At 0:40 the black clamp goes onto the negative post of the red car's battery under the yellow DANGER/POISON label (step-5.jpg).
At 0:42-0:46 the black clamp grips a bare metal bolt/bracket by the silver car's hood hinge near the windshield, above the leaves, away from the battery. The 'cables are live' caption is on screen.
At 0:48-0:50 the red car's ENGINE START/STOP button is pressed and its green light comes on. The step-7 frame shows the cluster lit with PARK.

edits.safety: Stay clear of the engine bays and keep the cables away from fans and belts while it starts.

why: At 0:52-0:58 the VW's START ENGINE STOP button is pressed and the tach rises. The 'three or four times in a row' limit isn't in the video. I made the line a plain hazard warning.

At 1:00-1:04 the clamps come off the red car's battery and at 1:06 the two men hold the clamps apart. From 1:08 it is driving footage and the troubleshooting slide (not steps). The reverse-order text is standard, though the video only clearly shows the red-car clamps coming off.
